residual_risks: The depth proxy uses a first-order Taylor approximation (sqrt(1+x) ~= 1 + x/2); bands up to 100% are accepted but the approximation error grows with band_bps. Downstream consumers may wish to bound band_bps to <= 500 bps for economically meaningful proxies; the contract forbids labelling the result as observed depth, so callers must treat it as a proxy.

Realised variance uses integer-arithmetic variance of sqrt-price ratios in Q64.64; a downstream consumer that wants realised volatility (sqrt of variance) must do so inside its own named float boundary (ADR-014 §5).

SwapObservation, ModifyLiquidityObservation, GasObservation and BlockHeaderObservation are minimal layer-local dataclasses; they deliberately do not import from robinhood_lp.storage so the features layer stays layer-pure. A future task may want a small adapter from the storage / replay schema to these observation types; that adapter does not belong to T050.

The MarketBarStreamer rejects window_end values that are not exact positive multiples of window_size. Streamers that want to build non-aligned windows (e.g. for irregular block spacing) must use the stateless compute_*_bar functions directly.

The freshness bar's semantics depend on the consumer truncating observations to those whose observed_at <= data_time. The test suite exercises this contract (test_freshness_bar_unchanged_by_future_event truncates before recomputing); a downstream consumer that passes future observations to compute_freshness_bar without truncating will see a freshness that depends on the future, breaking prefix invariance for that caller. This is documented in the compute_freshness_bar docstring.
